settings.heading: Sealed, because the routine is the product.
settings.lead: One set. Two formulas. Restore Balm for fresh work. Recovery Cream for the second stage and the months after.
settings.body: Every piece needs both, one after the other. No single product does the job, so they don’t come apart. Not as a discount. As a discipline.
settings.micro_1: Ships in 1–2 business days from Surfers Paradise

settings.eyebrow: The chemistry · Lists published in full
settings.heading: Tested. Not claimed.
settings.sub: In order, exactly as they read on the jar. Every batch tested in the lab, trialled in the chair. Not claimed.

settings.label: Step one · Days 1–14
settings.name: Restore Balm
settings.body: A concentrated balm that lays down a protective layer and holds moisture in while the work closes over. Thin layer, clean dry skin, morning and night.

settings.label: Step two · The months after
settings.name: Recovery Cream
settings.body: A lighter daily cream that sinks in fast to hydrate and soothe while the work settles. The stage most people skip. Don’t.

settings.heading: Two stages. Two formulas.
settings.intro: Fresh work needs sealing. Settling work needs conditioning. The balm is too heavy for the second stage. The cream is too light for the first.
settings.caption: Two textures. Two jobs.
settings.outro: Heavy, detailed work uses both, layered. Seventeen years in the chair says one product can’t do it. That is why they’re sealed together.

settings.heading: In their own words.
settings.sub: Collected by Judge.me after purchase. Published as written.

settings.heading: Built at the counter of a working studio.
settings.quote: Nothing goes on a client’s skin that has not been proven on my own first.
settings.attr_credential: Seventeen years under the needle · Still to this day
settings.body:
Every piece that leaves this counter comes back through it. We see what holds, what fades, and what it was looked after with. Hundreds of times a year.

Aftercare is usually made at a distance from the chair. This was made at the counter of a working studio, by the person who owns it — and it goes on his own skin before it goes on anyone else’s.

So we built the thing that couldn’t be bought.
settings.mono_line: Squires Ink · Orchid Avenue · Surfers Paradise

settings.heading: The artists it was built alongside.
settings.quote: What I recommend to my clients is formulas that work in hydrating the skin and look after my work long after it leaves the studio. Because this is my passion.
settings.attr_role: Large-scale realism · Squires Ink, Surfers Paradise
settings.body:
Calabria to the Gold Coast. Best Realism Piece, Caserta 2019. The artist currently working the founder’s chest, session after session, with the Ritual on the counter beside him.

No payment. No free product. No arrangement. His words are his own.

settings.heading: Built on discipline. Driven by purpose.
settings.quote: TEL isn’t a brand you buy once. It’s a standard you choose.
settings.body:
Most things are made to be good enough. TEL started on the opposite belief: that good enough is a decision, and so is everything better.

It starts with aftercare, because looking after the work is the work. It grows the way it began — chapter by chapter, each one earned before it’s named.

settings.heading: Five hundred sets.
settings.body: Chapter One is open. Five hundred sets, sealed, never sold apart. When they’re gone, it closes.
settings.closed_body: Five hundred sets, gone. Chapter Two — fragrance — is in development. The list hears first.

settings.heading: Our signature scent. One run.
settings.body: In development. The list gets the release date, the story behind it, and the doors 24 hours before they open to the public.
